title: Locked Increment
statement: Implement `solve(n)`. Return `n`, the total after incrementing a counter `n` times by 1 from 0. `n` is non-negative. The point of the lock is that the total equals the number of increments. This single-threaded function is that correct total.
hints: A loop of n increments is enough here.
The locked version has the same result.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Without a lock, two threads can read the same value and each write value+1, losing an increment.

editorial: Without a lock, two threads can read the same value and each write value+1, losing an increment. With a lock around the read-modify-write, n increments finish at n. This function returns that correct total. The lock does not change the arithmetic. It makes the arithmetic the one that happens.
